stem: In the figure, \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{BC}\), \(AD = 4\), \(DB = 6\), and \(DE = 5\). What is the length of \(\overline{BC}\)?
solution: Because \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), triangle \(ADE\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(5 \cdot \frac{4}{10}\); the ratio is inverted, which makes \(BC\) shorter than \(DE\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(5 \cdot \frac{6}{4}\); it compares \(DB\) to \(AD\), but the similar triangles have sides \(AB = 10\) and \(AD = 4\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This adds 6 to \(DE\); similar triangles scale lengths by multiplying, not by adding.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(d('A','D')-4)<0.01 and abs(d('D','B')-6)<0.01 and abs(d('D','E')-5)<0.01 and P['D'][1]==P['E'][1] and P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]
ans=Rational(5)*(4+6)/4
assert abs(d('B','C')-ans)<0.01
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==Rational(25,2)
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
